candidates.review_note: Maintain one binary trie for each divisor, inserting each distinct value into tries for exactly its divisors. k must divide x; then the required gcd condition reduces to v being in trie k. Store minimum numeric value per subtree so greedy opposite-bit traversal only selects branches containing v<=s-x. Compact arrays and duplicate suppression bound memory; no answer exists if the root minimum exceeds the sum budget.

Split integers uniquely into c*2^a*3^b with gcd(c,6)=1. Each component is a staircase grid whose horizontal/vertical neighbors cannot both be selected. Row-profile independent-set DP uses subset zeta sums for disjoint-row compatibility. Component shape changes only at2^a3^b thresholds, so cache by the preceding smooth number. Quotient grouping counts all coprime-to6 roots without iterating every integer for every query.

Use F(depth+shift)=F(depth)*F(shift-1)+F(depth+1)*F(shift), including signed-index Fibonacci for updates beginning below their index. Heavy-light order makes every subtree contiguous and every path logarithmically many intervals. Lazy segment updates add two coefficients against fixed sums of depth-basis values. Fast doubling handles k up to1e15; iterative tree processing avoids deep-tree recursion.

Safe positions satisfy a^b<n. For a>=2 the game is finite; descending DP marks a position winning iff a safe increment reaches a losing position. Exponent>=2 has only O(sqrt(n)) total-scale base ranges, while the long b=1 tail permits only base increments and is solved by parity. At a=1, arbitrarily increasing b eventually allows an infinite draw; propagate win/loss/draw backward instead of imposing a false finite cutoff.

Parity prefix sums generate the exact column recurrence for all positive odd jump lengths and the three allowed destination rows. The finite transfer system has order at most2n+1 including the initial impulse. Berlekamp-Massey over prime30011 recovers this recurrence from more than twice that many exact terms; polynomial exponentiation computes column m-1 in O(n^2 log m), retaining the special starting column.
